question.text: Which of the following is NOT a valid purpose for creating a trust in estate planning?

answer.text: Tax evasion through concealment of assets
Ensuring systematic distribution of wealth over time
Providing for dependents with special needs

explanation.text: The Logic: Tax evasion — the illegal concealment of income or assets to avoid lawful tax — is never a valid purpose for creating a trust. Trusts in estate planning are legitimately used to protect assets for minor beneficiaries, provide for dependents with special needs, ensure systematic distribution of wealth over time, and create tax-efficient structures for orderly wealth transfer. Tax-efficient planning (legal) is distinct from tax evasion (illegal). The Trap: Options A, C, and D all describe well-recognised legitimate trust purposes — protecting minors, systematic distribution, and providing for special-needs dependents. Only option B describes an illegal objective that no estate-planning trust may validly pursue. Note: The Retirement Adviser workbook discusses creating tax-efficient trust structures to manage the estate and make periodic payouts, but the explicit 'tax evasion / concealment' framing in the keyed answer was not located in the cited pages. The framing above reflects general legal and tax-planning principles rather than a direct workbook citation.
